claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Pack cementation at approximately 900–1000 °C for several hours can aluminize the surface of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminization treatment will produce a thin, continuous, dense, and adherent Al2O3 surface scale.
Al introduced at the alloy surface will preferentially oxidize upon oxygen exposure.
Preferential oxidation of surface Al will form a stable alumina layer.
A continuous Al2O3 scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The alumina barrier will dramatically slow oxygen ingress into the HfNbTaTiZr bulk.
Slower oxygen ingress will preserve the alloy's internal microstructure.
Preservation of the internal microstructure will preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
Relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, aluminized material will exhibit significantly lower oxygen uptake during high-temperature exposure.
Relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, aluminized material will exhibit less oxide-layer penetration during high-temperature exposure.
After exposure in air at approximately 1000 °C for about 100 hours, the aluminized alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
At 1000 °C and strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, the aluminized alloy will retain a yield strength within 163–530 MPa.
A scale that is excessively thick or that spalls under thermal cycling or mechanical stress could compromise mechanical performance.
Bulk compositional changes or diffusion caused by aluminization could alter the alloy microstructure.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and intervention imply that pack cementation itself forms the alumina scale, whereas the mechanism says aluminization first introduces surface Al and that alumina forms subsequently upon oxygen exposure.

The falsification rule treats any yield strength outside 163–530 MPa as adverse, even though a value above 530 MPa would not necessarily constitute degradation and could exceed the stated baseline performance.
